findings.item: R3-1: section 13 Rust bullet says 'as before' without naming the baseline
findings.detail: 'Rust: a target rust compile gives the same typed prompt, DSL and product files as before. Its bundle differs only in two descriptors and in payload_sha256' is true against the current default (candidate-006), but not against run-003, whose shared compiler-v1 descriptors predate amendment 004. The acceptance bullets and the plan already say 'current default', so this is not ambiguous for acceptance. Saying 'as the current default' in that bullet would match the Python bullet. This is optional and does not block.

findings.item: R2-1: acceptance-plan.json amendment005 'Rust compile' and 'Rust recordings' checks use a baseline that cannot satisfy them (rust-output-055 run-003)
findings.detail: Both checks compare the candidate against 'every recorded Rust compile response' or 'every recorded Rust bundle' of rust-output-055 run-003, and both fail. (a) run-003 does not keep Rust compile responses or bundles. phase2/cases/*.json keep only compile_sha256, bundle_sha256 and files_sha256 under 'rust'. rust-products.json (phase 1) keeps only bundle_payload_sha256 and files_sha256. A grep for som.dsl-bundle.v2 in run-003 outside the cargo target and work dirs finds only header, summary, health and CLI artefacts. A comparison 'except backend, target_contract and payload_sha256' cannot be computed from a hash, and no recorded bundle exists to send and rebase. issue57 run-004 does not keep Rust bundles either. (b) Even if the bytes existed, run-003 ran on rust-output-candidate-004, before compiler-v1 amendment 003 / rust-output-v1 amendment 004. A Rust bundle carries the shared compiler-v1 descriptors (som-targets/src/rust/mod.rs descriptors() starts from compiler.descriptors(prompt); ASSET_KEYS includes compiler_contract and selection_policy). Those changed with amendment 004: python_unchanged amendment_004 admits compiler_contract and selection_policy, and A6_amendment_004 recomputes the shared descriptors. So the current candidate's Rust bundles also differ from run-003 in those descriptors, and the claims 'only backend and target_contract differ' and 'except bundle.assets.backend, bundle.assets.target_contract and hashes.payload_sha256' are false against run-003. They are true only against the current default (#57 release, candidate-006). Each check blocks acceptance, so #65 could never be accepted without another amendment. This is the same class of problem as round 1 finding 1. Fix (the Rust analog of the new Python check): baseline both checks on the current default. Compile every phase 1 and phase 2 Rust case of run-003's inventory with target rust read-only against the current default, and require that the candidate's response equal it except bundle.assets.backend, bundle.assets.target_contract and bundle.hashes.payload_sha256 (RS12/RS13: equal compiler-v1 refusal bytes). Then send those current-default bundles to the candidate's assemble, require ASSET_HASH_MISMATCH at /bundle/assets, and require that the same bundles, rebased on the candidate's descriptors (only backend and target_contract replaced, payload rehashed), assemble to the files run-003 recorded (files_sha256). Keep check_rust_unchanged.py against run-003 as written, because it compares files_sha256, which run-003 does keep. Also update the matching section 13 acceptance bullets ('equals the recorded one', 'every recorded Rust bundle').
findings.resolution: RESOLVED in round 3. acceptance-plan.json amendment005 gains a 'baseline' key: rust-output-candidate-006, binary 52658e13..., build commit 6116fed5..., release evidence rust-output-release-2026-10-20-issue57.json, read only. 'Rust compile against the baseline' compares the candidate with the baseline's response for the run-003 inventory, except backend, target_contract and payload_sha256, and requires RS12/RS13 to give the baseline's refusal bytes. This is satisfiable because the shared compiler-v1 descriptors and the Rust catalog, block_library and formatter are unchanged against candidate-006. 'Rust bundles of the baseline' refuses the baseline's bundles with ASSET_HASH_MISMATCH and assembles them, rebased on backend and target_contract, to run-003's files_sha256. That data exists: phase 1 rust-products.json and phase2/cases files_sha256. Bundles exist for 582 of the 584 phase 2 cases plus the phase 1 cases; RS12/RS13 return refusals, so they have none, which matches 'every Rust bundle the baseline returns'. check_rust_unchanged.py against run-003 is kept. The section 13 acceptance bullets now say current default and run-003.

findings.item: acceptance-plan.json amendment005 check 3 (python_unchanged) cannot pass as written
findings.detail: The check requires 'python_replay.py without --asset-break over the 127 public products (public-products-003b) and the 544 legacy jobs (legacy544 run-005)'. Those recorded exchanges predate compiler-v1 amendment 003. The issue57 acceptance (rust-output-acceptance-2026-10-20-issue57.json results.python_replay.mode) had to use asset_break true, with 671 recorded bundles refused with ASSET_HASH_MISMATCH and 671 rebased assembles. The default on 8765 is now that post-amendment-004 build (rust-output-release-2026-10-20-issue57.json). Without --asset-break, python_replay.py requires byte-identical compile responses, so every compile and assemble exchange on any post-004 candidate (including the first TS phase 1 candidate) fails by construction. The check would block #65 or force another amendment. Fix: compare against the current accepted default, for example with a new Python baseline recorded from the post-004 default and named in the plan, or check_targets.py --reference against the default without --asset-break, with python_replay byte comparison against that baseline. Or keep --asset-break for the old recordings and also require that the candidate's Python compile responses equal the current default's byte for byte. Update section 13 'That covers the 127 public products and the 544 historical jobs' to name the baseline.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED. The new 'Python against the current default' check requires byte-for-byte compile and assemble equality with the current default (the #57 release) for the 127 public and 544 legacy prompts, with no target and with target python. This is satisfiable because the Python manifest (som-rs/src/compiler.rs backend_manifest) does not depend on som-targets. The separate 'Python recordings' check keeps python_replay.py --asset-break with the amendment_004 rule. Section 13 names the baselines.

Fix: baseline them on the current default as the Python check now does. New minor R2-2: the draft says 'Sealed' and lists the descriptors inconsistently. The receipt (8c25078c...5d51) is intact and consistent. check_contract and cargo test show only the expected status-driven failures. R2-2 (draft sealed claim, 11 ASSET_KEYS) and R2-3 (baseline pinned) are resolved. No blocker or major remains. Only an optional wording note (R3-1) is open.
